title: Backlog Clarity Bootcamp — Sprint 24 Prioritization & Cut Decisions
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a lightweight working doc for the "Backlog Clarity" half-day session we ran on Nov 5. Goal: reduce sprint-24 scope by ~30% while preserving high-impact deployables (observability, route rules, and rollout experience). This doc captures the decisions we made, the rough rationales, quick UX wireframe notes, and follow-ups (who owns the todos + suggested Jira next-steps).

Summary of outcomes (headline):
- Confirmed MUST / SHOULD / NICE-to-have split for 18 candidate items -> reduced to 12 for Sprint 24 (engineering capacity limited due to infra migrations).
- Fast-fail items (non-blocking experiments) moved to backlog with clear success metrics.
- Identified 3 cross-team blockers needing SRE/Infra sync (see blockers section).

Attendees:
- Liam Chen (owner, product)
- Aisha Patel (PM, rollouts)
- Sofia Martinez (UX)
- Noah Walker (Eng lead, backend)
- Evan Brooks (SRE)
- plus notes from weekly console guild

Inputs considered before session:
- Sprint velocity report (past 4 sprints): avg 46 story points
- Console customer escalations list (top pain: rollout visibility, cost attribution)
- Playbook for canary rollouts: open issues CON-847, CON-903

Principles used for prioritization (agreed):
1) Customer impact first: things that remove blockers for paying Dedicated customers or unblock Private onboarding.
2) Production reliability wins over new bells (if reliability can materially reduce tickets).
3) Low-effort high-impact: prefer 1-3 day tasks with direct user-facing benefit.
4) Preserve at least one mid-sized UX polish task per sprint to keep momentum on product feel.

Candidate items reviewed (short list + immediate call):
1) Route table visualization overhaul (wireframe A) — estimate 8 sp, decision: SHOULD -> keep, split into backend API (5sp) + UI surface (3sp) for partial delivery.
2) Token-level cost breakdown per request (backend + console) — estimate 5 sp, decision: MUST -> move to top. Reason: frequent CS asks and directly helps cost debugging.
3) Rollout canary failure email alerts (templated) — estimate 3 sp, decision: MUST -> quick win for Enterprise.
4) In-console model variant comparison panel (experimental) — estimate 8 sp, decision: NICE -> defer to sprint 25 unless capacity opens.
5) Per-route latency percentiles (90/95/99) in chart view — estimate 5 sp, decision: SHOULD -> keep, but scope down to 90/95 only (defer 99).
6) Bulk route import CSV uploader — estimate 5 sp, decision: NICE -> defer (low usage signals).
7) KV cache evictions visualizer (DEBUG-level) — estimate 4 sp, decision: MUST if SRE signs off; action: Evan to confirm impact.
8) Quick onboarding checklist for new orgs (docs + in-console) — estimate 3 sp, decision: SHOULD -> keep as 2-day UX + 1-day doc.
9) Rollout audit stream replay (backend) — estimate 8 sp, decision: NICE -> defer.
10) Model pinning API expansion (allow tags) — estimate 6 sp, decision: SHOULD -> split; API (4sp) first, UI later.
11) Query-level debug share link (expiring URLs) — estimate 3 sp, decision: MUST -> high impact for support.
12) A/B rollout funnel telemetry (proto) — estimate 8 sp, decision: NICE -> move to alpha backlog.

Sprint 24 proposed commitment (after cuts):
- Token-level cost breakdown per request (CON-903) — 5sp (priority 1) — owner: Liam/NW
- Rollout canary failure email alerts — 3sp (priority 1) — owner: Aisha
- Query-level debug share link — 3sp (priority 1) — owner: Noah
- Route table visualization (backend API slice) — 5sp (priority 2) — owner: Noah
- Per-route latency percentiles (90/95 only) — 5sp (priority 2) — owner: Evan
- Quick onboarding checklist (UX + doc) — 3sp (priority 2) — owner: Sofia
Total planned: 24 story points (we left buffer ~6 sp for interrupts).

Wireframe & UX notes (Sofia):
- Route table visualization (wireframe A)
  - Minimal first-pass: table + mini-sparkline, click-to-expand modal with route config preview. Avoid heavy canvas work this sprint.
  - Key interactions: sort by error-rate, filter by model-family, inline rollout status chips.
  - Accessibility: ensure chip color doesn't convey meaning alone (add icon + text).

- Token-cost breakdown panel
  - Inline accordion per-request showing model, tokens-in, tokens-out, cost-per-token, estimated cost-savings tips (e.g., suggest quantized variant).
  - User research note: rollout folks requested copy-to-clipboard CSV export for sharing with finance. Quick MVP: export button that dumps visible table.

Open blockers / risks:
- Infra migration (GPU host naming) scheduled by infra team week of Nov 8 -> may reduce available capacity for console QA. Evan to confirm.
- SSO auth token rotation plan unclear – could break some debug-share workflows. Owner: Security team (we will escalate if not resolved by Nov 10).
- Some backend endpoints required for route table API are owned by platform-engineering; need an explicit sync. Action: Liam to schedule 30-min alignment meeting with platform-engineering (CON-847 referenced).

Dropped items and rationale (moved to backlog):
- In-console model variant comparison panel (experimental) — low telemetry + high UI effort. Moved to product backlog with label "needs-data".
- Bulk route import CSV uploader — not enough customer asks; ticket archived for now.
- Rollout audit stream replay — engineering-heavy and lower immediate customer value.

Short-term todos (owners + due dates):
- Evan: confirm SRE gating for KV cache visualizer (by 2026-11-09) -> if yes, convert to MUST and slot in sprint.
- Liam: create consolidated sprint plan + update Jira sprint (target 2026-11-08).
- Aisha: draft alert email copy + template (shared doc) (target 2026-11-06).
- Sofia: produce clickable mock for route table modal (Figma link in CONfluence) (target 2026-11-09).

Communication plan:
- Post summary to #console-prod channel with the sprint scope and rationale (Liam) on Nov 7.
- Send heads-up to customer-success + solutions-engineering about changes to onboarding checklist; request feedback by Nov 10.

Appendix: Quick decision logs and artifacts
- Decision: limit percentile telemetry to 90/95 this sprint to reduce compute load (NW + Evan).
- Decision: prefer API-first delivery on large features so we can ship iterative UI slices.
- Quick links:
  - CON-903 (token cost breakdown): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CON-903
  - CON-847 (route table API): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CON-847
  - Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxx/console-route-table-v1 (Sofia owns)

Notes to self (Liam) — informal: 
- Keep an eye on infra freeze windows, that is the usual sprint killer.
- Next session: bring 2-3 customer quotes that directly map to items to make prioritization less fuzzy.

If anything in this doc is unclear, ping me (Liam) or update the doc and tag "@Aisha" for rollout items.
